author.name: Reliability Ruth
author.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.

challenge.name: The Committed Pallets
challenge.description: A supplier has confirmed a bulk order for a middle aisle promotion that ships next week, leaving no room for model error. #requirements_reuben# insists the acceptance criteria must be fully governed to guarantee the allocation logic is auditable before the trucks leave. #reliability_ruth# argues the criteria are sufficient as manual checks because the physical stock is already committed and the team needs to ship the feature immediately to handle the live orders.

output.content: We cannot wait for a full governance sign off before the trucks leave. The supplier has confirmed the bulk order, and the pallets are already committed to the distribution centre. If the allocation logic is not live by Friday, we will miss the promotion week entirely. I am willing to accept manual checks on the acceptance criteria for this specific release. The team will verify the output by hand against the committed stock levels. This ensures the feature is available for the live orders without delay. We will document these manual verifications for the audit trail. The physical stock is fixed, so the risk of model error is contained. We need to ship now to handle the immediate demand.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are willing to accept manual checks in place of full governance sign-off to meet the deadline, indicating a conscious sacrifice of process rigor for speed.
